subject: Archaeology
title: The Atocha: Florida's Treasure Ship
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Atocha: Florida's Treasure Ship usable.

hook.text: The Nuestra Señora de Atocha sank in a hurricane in 1622 carrying 40 tons of gold and silver. It took 16 years to find.

buildup.text: Mel Fisher spent 16 years and his life savings searching for the Atocha off the Florida Keys.

discovery.text: In 1985, his team found the mother lode: gold bars, silver coins, emeralds, and gold chains worth over $450 million.

twist.text: The state of Florida sued Fisher for the treasure. The case went to the Supreme Court, which ruled the treasure was his.

climax.text: Critics argued that treasure hunters destroy archaeological context. Fisher's team kept no proper excavation records.

punchline.text: He found $450 million in gold. He lost the history it could have told.

quiz.question: Why did archaeologists criticize Mel Fisher's Atocha recovery?
options: He sold the treasure to private collectors instead of museums
His team kept no proper excavation records, destroying archaeological context
He used explosives that damaged the wreck site
